items.stem: Which of these is a paradigm of learning?
items.answer: Operant conditioning
items.markingKey: (a) Operant conditioning.
options: Operant conditioning
Fatigue
Growth
Maturation

items.stem: Distinguish between 'learning' and 'performance'.
items.answer: Learning: any relatively permanent change in behaviour or behavioural potential produced by experience. Performance: the observed behaviour of a person, from which learning is inferred.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: 1 mark for explaining 'learning' (any relatively permanent change in behaviour or behavioural potential produced by experience.) and 1 mark for 'performance' (the observed behaviour of a person, from which learning is inferred.), with the contrast between them made clear.

items.stem: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
items.answer: Skill learning – learning by watching a model
items.markingKey: (a) Skill learning – learning by watching a model is wrong: Skill learning goes with learning a smooth sequence of responses through practice.
options: Skill learning – learning by watching a model
Classical conditioning – learning by association of two stimuli
Cognitive learning – learning through insight and understanding
Operant conditioning – learning from the consequences of behaviour

items.stem: The following statement about nature of learning and paradigms of learning is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "Changes in behaviour due to drugs are an example of learning."
items.answer: Such changes are temporary and are not learning.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (Such changes are temporary and are not learning.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: Read the case and answer. After running a race, Arjun walks slowly for an hour; the next day he is back to his normal pace. Identify the concept illustrated.
items.answer: Temporary change due to fatigue, not learning.

items.stem: "Learning is called an inferred process." Examine this statement with reference to nature of learning and paradigms of learning.
items.answer: The statement is valid. It cannot be observed directly and is judged from changes in performance.

items.answer: The time relation between the conditioned and unconditioned stimulus affects the speed of conditioning.

In Pavlov's experiment, food was the conditioned stimulus.
Backward conditioning is the most effective arrangement.

items.stem: Explain the determinants of classical conditioning.
items.answer: Time relations between stimuli; type of unconditioned stimulus – appetitive or aversive; intensity of conditioned stimulus; examples.

items.stem: "Delayed conditioning is the most effective arrangement." Examine this statement with reference to classical conditioning.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on classical conditioning and answer the questions that follow.
"Aversive unconditioned stimuli, such as electric shock, usually produce faster conditioning than appetitive ones. Many fears and phobias are acquired through classical conditioning. The time relation between the conditioned and unconditioned stimulus affects the speed of conditioning."
(i) A child conditioned to fear a white rat also fears a white rabbit. This is: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'backward conditioning' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: A child may become afraid of the doctor's clinic. (2)
items.answer: (i) stimulus generalisation (ii) The arrangement in which the unconditioned stimulus is presented before the conditioned stimulus. (iii) The clinic has been paired with the pain of injections, which is an unconditioned stimulus.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) stimulus generalisation (ii) The arrangement in which the unconditioned stimulus is presented before the conditioned stimulus. (iii) The clinic has been paired with the pain of injections, which is an unconditioned stimulus.

(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: Delayed conditioning is the most effective arrangement. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "Extinction means the learnt response is permanently erased." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (2)
items.answer: (i) The arrangement in which the unconditioned stimulus is presented before the conditioned stimulus. (ii) The conditioned stimulus reliably signals that the unconditioned stimulus is about to come. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: An extinguished response can reappear through spontaneous recovery.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) The arrangement in which the unconditioned stimulus is presented before the conditioned stimulus. (ii) The conditioned stimulus reliably signals that the unconditioned stimulus is about to come. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: An extinguished response can reappear through spontaneous recovery.

items.stem:
Read the following statements about nature of learning and paradigms of learning:
I. Learning is an inferred process and is different from performance.
II. Learning paradigms include classical and operant conditioning, observational, cognitive, verbal, concept and skill learning.
III. Changes due to fatigue, habituation, drugs or maturation are not learning.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: All of them
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is correct. III is correct.
options: III only
II only
All of them
I and II only

items.stem: Distinguish between 'shaping' and 'schedule of reinforcement'.
items.answer: Shaping: reinforcing successive approximations to the desired response. Schedule of reinforcement: the arrangement of when and how often reinforcement is given.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: 1 mark for explaining 'shaping' (reinforcing successive approximations to the desired response.) and 1 mark for 'schedule of reinforcement' (the arrangement of when and how often reinforcement is given.), with the contrast between them made clear.

items.stem:
Read the following statements about classical conditioning:
I. The time relation between the conditioned and unconditioned stimulus affects the speed of conditioning.
II. Backward conditioning is the most effective arrangement.
III. Extinction means the learnt response is permanently erased.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: I only
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is incorrect: Delayed conditioning is the most effective; backward conditioning is the least effective. III is incorrect: An extinguished response can reappear through spontaneous recovery.
options: II only
All of them
I only
II and III only

items.stem:
Read the following extract on observational, cognitive, verbal, concept and skill learning and answer the questions that follow.
"In insight learning the solution comes suddenly and can be applied to similar problems. Concepts may be artificial, with clearly defined features, or natural, with fuzzy boundaries. Skill learning passes through cognitive, associative and autonomous phases."
(i) The study in which children imitated aggression towards a doll after watching a film was conducted by: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'transfer of learning' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Children copy the behaviour of characters they see on television. (2)
items.answer: (i) Albert Bandura (ii) The effect of earlier learning on later learning, which may be positive, negative or zero. (iii) People learn by observing models and the consequences of their behaviour.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) Albert Bandura (ii) The effect of earlier learning on later learning, which may be positive, negative or zero. (iii) People learn by observing models and the consequences of their behaviour.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about factors facilitating learning and learning disabilities:
I. Motivation, whether intrinsic or extrinsic, facilitates learning.
II. Learning disabilities are not the result of intellectual disability or sensory impairment alone.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: Both I and II
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is correct.
options: I only
II only
Both I and II
Neither I nor II

items.stem: What is meant by 'paradigm of learning' in the context of nature of learning and paradigms of learning?
items.answer: A distinct type or method of learning, such as classical conditioning, operant conditioning or observational learning.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: paradigm of learning correctly explained as a distinct type or method of learning, such as classical conditioning, operant conditioning or observational learning.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): An extinguished response may reappear after a rest.
Reason (R): Extinction weakens the response without erasing the learnt association completely.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both are true and R explains A: extinction weakens the response without erasing the learnt association completely.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about operant conditioning is NOT correct?
items.answer: Continuous reinforcement makes responses most resistant to extinction.
items.markingKey: (b) It is incorrect. Partial reinforcement makes responses more resistant to extinction.
options: Delayed reinforcement is less effective than immediate reinforcement.
Continuous reinforcement makes responses most resistant to extinction.
Both positive and negative reinforcement increase the probability of a response.
Punishment decreases the probability of a response.

items.stem: Read the case and answer. A man keeps buying lottery tickets for years although he wins only now and then, after an unpredictable number of tickets. Name the schedule of reinforcement shown here and explain it briefly.
items.answer: Variable ratio schedule: reinforcement after a varying number of responses produces high, steady responding resistant to extinction.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: 1 mark for naming it (variable ratio schedule); 1 mark for the explanation (reinforcement after a varying number of responses produces high, steady responding resistant to extinction).

items.stem:
Statement: Partial reinforcement facilitates lasting learning.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: Responses learnt under partial reinforcement are more resistant to extinction.
items.markingKey: (b) Responses learnt under partial reinforcement are more resistant to extinction.
options: Learning disabilities affect specific abilities such as reading and writing.
Responses learnt under partial reinforcement are more resistant to extinction.
Each learner has a learning style for responding to and using stimuli.
They had already formed a cognitive map of the maze through latent learning.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about nature of learning and paradigms of learning is correct?
items.answer: Learning is an inferred process and is different from performance.
items.markingKey: (c) The others are wrong: Maturation is due to biological growth, not experience. Learning is inferred from performance, which may not always reflect what has been learnt. Such changes are temporary and are not learning.
options: Learning and performance are the same.
Changes due to maturation are a kind of learning.
Learning is an inferred process and is different from performance.
Changes in behaviour due to drugs are an example of learning.

items.stem:
Match List I with List II and choose the correct option.
List I:
A. Observational learning
B. Verbal learning
C. Latent learning
D. Insight learning
List II:
1. Tolman's rats forming a cognitive map of a maze
2. Kohler's chimpanzees reaching bananas with sticks
3. Ebbinghaus's nonsense syllables
4. Bandura's study of children copying aggression
items.markingKey: (c) Observational learning – Bandura's study of children copying aggression; Verbal learning – Ebbinghaus's nonsense syllables; Latent learning – Tolman's rats forming a cognitive map of a maze; Insight learning – Kohler's chimpanzees reaching bananas with sticks.

items.stem: A child conditioned to fear a white rat also fears a white rabbit. This is:
items.answer: stimulus generalisation
items.markingKey: (c) stimulus generalisation.
options: spontaneous recovery
extinction
stimulus generalisation
discrimination

items.stem: Read the case and answer. After being stung once, a boy now fears not only bees but also wasps and flies. Name the process in conditioning shown here and explain it briefly.
items.answer: Stimulus generalisation: responses spread to stimuli similar to the conditioned stimulus.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: 1 mark for naming it (stimulus generalisation); 1 mark for the explanation (responses spread to stimuli similar to the conditioned stimulus).

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about factors facilitating learning and learning disabilities is NOT correct?
items.answer: Extrinsic motivation is learning for the joy of the activity.
items.markingKey: (a) It is incorrect. That is intrinsic motivation; extrinsic is learning for external rewards.
options: Extrinsic motivation is learning for the joy of the activity.
Children with learning disabilities may show poor spatial orientation and motor coordination.
Learning disabilities are not the result of intellectual disability or sensory impairment alone.
Learning disabilities can be remedied through suitable intervention and teaching methods.

items.stem:
Statement: Changes in behaviour due to fatigue are not learning.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: They are temporary and not produced by experience.
items.markingKey: (c) They are temporary and not produced by experience.
options: It cannot be observed directly and is judged from changes in performance.
Extinction weakens the response without erasing the learnt association completely.
They are temporary and not produced by experience.
People learn by observing models and the consequences of their behaviour.
